title: Docs: tighten API key creation + env var setup; add 401/403 troubleshooting
author: Wei Chen
description: Context: We’re seeing a consistent cluster of onboarding tickets and quickstart drop-off related to API key setup (wrong key, key copied with whitespace, env var not loaded in shell/CI, using the wrong header). This PR tightens the API key + environment variable docs to be more explicit and adds a troubleshooting section focused on the most common 401/403 patterns (mapped to Support macros). This is a prerequisite for the Console onboarding checklist deep links so the checklist step can send users to a single canonical page. Changes: (1) Clarify ‘Create an API key’ flow with explicit callouts about key visibility (shown once), key naming, and least-privilege guidance where applicable. (2) Standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY as the canonical env var name across docs and quickstarts; include a compatibility note for OPENAI_API_KEY only in the OpenAI-compat docs (not on the core API key page). (3) Add copy/paste-safe examples for Bash/Zsh/Fish, PowerShell, Docker, GitHub Actions, and Vercel/Render style secret config; include a quick verification snippet that prints the presence (not the value) and then performs a minimal /v1/models request. (4) Add a dedicated “Troubleshooting 401/403” section with a decision tree: 401 invalid_api_key vs 401 missing_authorization_header vs 403 key_revoked/disabled vs 403 project_not_allowed vs 403 org_policy; includes how to rotate keys and what to send Support (request-id + timestamp + region) without sharing the key. (5) Tighten language around common gotchas: ‘export REDWOOD_API_KEY=…’ must be in the same shell session, no quotes that get included in value, avoid trailing newline when copying from password managers, and ensure the key belongs to the same workspace/project as the Console UI you’re using. (6) Update redirects and cross-links from quickstarts so “Set your API key” points here rather than multiple legacy pages. Notes: No product behavior changes; doc-only. This is intentionally opinionated about env var naming to reduce mismatch across examples and telemetry attribution (checklist funnel). Follow-ups: we should update older blog/README references to OPENAI_API_KEY separately (tracked in ENG-5831 subtask).
commits: docs(auth): rewrite API key creation + setup page with canonical env var
docs(auth): add 401/403 troubleshooting matrix + support-friendly guidance
docs(quickstarts): update cross-links and redirects to canonical setup page
docs(ci): add GitHub Actions secret example + minimal verification call
review_conversation: Elliot Price (review): Can we avoid having both REDWOOD_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY on the same page? We’ve been trying to keep the core path clean for hosted users.

Wei Chen (author): Yep — I moved OPENAI_API_KEY references to the OpenAI-compat doc only and added a short note + link from the main page (“Using OpenAI-compatible clients?”). Core page now only uses REDWOOD_API_KEY.

Dev Patel (review): Troubleshooting section is great. Can you add a very explicit callout that users should not paste the key value into tickets, and tell them what metadata to provide instead (request-id, approximate time, region)?
Wei Chen (author): Added an info box in the troubleshooting page and mirrored the same language on the API key page. Also included an example of what to send Support.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): For the 403 cases, let’s be careful about implying “scope” if we don’t expose per-scope keys to all tenants yet. Suggest wording like “key disabled / workspace policy / project restrictions”. Also: can we mention that API keys are workspace-bound and that switching workspaces in Console is a common source of confusion?

Wei Chen (author): Updated the 403 copy to avoid “scope” language and added a “workspace mismatch” bullet with a screenshot alt-text reference (no image in repo) and precise Console steps (“check workspace selector in top-left”).

Priya Shah (review): In SUP-18421 we saw users include quotes: export REDWOOD_API_KEY="rk_...". That’s fine in bash, but some copy/paste ends up including smart quotes from docs. Please ensure we use plain quotes or avoid quotes entirely.
Wei Chen (author): Examples now avoid quotes entirely unless necessary; where we do show quotes (PowerShell), it’s plain ASCII. Also added a note about smart quotes when copying from rich text.
Elliot Price (final review): Looks good. Please add one more verification snippet that checks the env var is set without echoing it (we’ve had people paste screenshots).
Wei Chen (author): Added `python -c` and `node -e` one-liners that only print “set/not set”, plus a curl call that returns HTTP status + request-id header.
release_notes: Docs: consolidated API key + environment variable setup into a single canonical path
Docs: added 401/403 troubleshooting guide (common causes + fixes) aligned with Support macros
